title: Chapter 6 — Election Day
description: Three polling units, ballot snatchers, Mama Titi's market, and a long night of counting.

cards.title: Election Day
cards.text: 6:00 a.m. No movement. No okada, no danfo, no Task Force. Just the queues, and the birds, who are confused.

beats.speaker: seyi
beats.text: Three polling units decide everything: the Front Stop, the Market and the Motor Park. Go to each one. Show your face. Make sure the agents are awake and the boxes are where we left them.

variants.text: (He looks at the empty passenger seat.) Three polling units decide everything: the Front Stop, the Market and the Motor Park. Funke is not answering my calls either, if it helps.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The queue at the Front Stop is three hundred people long. An old man is sitting on a bucket, refusing to leave until he votes. "I voted in 1979," he says. "I will vote again before I die."

options.text: Bring him water and a chair from the tea table.
Shake his hand for the cameras.
Ask your agent to make sure he votes first.

beats.speaker: mamaTiti
beats.text: Teacher! The women are here. All of them. We are voting for the toilet. (She shows you a padlock.) This is the key Owó Ńlá never gave us. I bought a new lock for your own.

beats.speaker: mamaTiti
beats.text: The association remembers, Teacher. (She doesn't smile.) We will see if you remember too.

beats.speaker: mamaTiti
beats.text: They are voting for the notebook. (She shows you. The women have written in it. Pages and pages.) Don't lose it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: At the Motor Park polling unit, three boys in black are running towards the ballot box. One of them has a cutlass. The INEC officer has disappeared under a table.

beats.speaker: babaTicket
beats.text: (From the ticket office window.) Teacher! Na your box dem wan carry!

won.toast: The box stays. The drivers carry you on their shoulders.

beats.headline: COUNTING IN PROGRESS
beats.text: Results are coming in from the polling units. The collation centre has asked everybody to remain calm, and has locked its door from the inside.

beats.headline: BREAKING: THE "LOGISTICS" TAPE
beats.text: Wahala FM has received a recording of a commission official explaining how wards 4, 7 and 9 were "already settled". Ifeoma Nwankwo will be playing it in full, every hour, until somebody arrests somebody.

beats.headline: THE OKO FILES
beats.text: Fourteen contracts. Twelve companies. One director. Wahala FM can reveal that Mr. Wale Oko has built nothing, nine times, for ₦300 million. Baba Oko could not be reached. His Prado was seen heading towards the airport.

beats.title: Election Day
beats.summary: The boxes are counted. Somewhere in a locked room, a man in a safari suit is adding up what you are worth.
